avalancheActivity.comment: The main issue is fresh snow at the highest elevations. We expect 10–15 cm of fresh snow. Be cautious in very steep areas, narrow gullies, slopes beneath rock faces, and terrain depressions where snow has been blown by the wind into snow pillows, slabs, and drifts. Prolonged low temperatures and a thin snowpack are leading to the development of critical—permanently weak—layers within the snowpack. Avalanches may be triggered primarily by significant additional loading, though the occurrence of smaller spontaneous avalanches from fresh snow cannot be ruled out.
avalancheActivity.highlights: Watch out for fresh snow at high elevations!

snowpackStructure.comment: Cold air of Arctic origin continues to linger over Slovakia, bringing snowfall from the north accompanied by strong NW to S winds. Over the past 3 days, 10 to 30 cm of new snow has fallen; a continuous snowpack is present starting from the foothills, with significant depths found above the tree line, where it reaches 30 to 70 cm, and locally even more. Partly due to low temperatures, the snow layers are not sufficiently bonded together. Due to the wind, the snow cover is distributed very unevenly.

avalancheActivity.comment: We expect 10–15 cm of fresh snow, which may pose a risk, especially in areas with an older snowpack. Under additional weight, small avalanches may be triggered on steep slopes.
avalancheActivity.highlights: Watch out for fresh snow above the tree line.

snowpackStructure.comment: We expect 10–15 cm of new snow, which will fall in some places on top of layers of older, wind-blown snow. Within the snowpack, there are weak layers of angular-grained snow. Due to low temperatures, the snowpack will stabilize only slowly.
